# Prebuilt Binaries

This archive ships with ready-to-run binaries under `bin/`, so you can try the
harness without a Rust toolchain.

## What's included

| File | Target | Build | Size | Runs on |
|------|--------|-------|------|---------|
| `bin/inbharat-harness` | x86_64-unknown-linux-musl | release (optimized, stripped) | ~947 KB | Any x86_64 Linux — fully static, no libc dependency (musl). **Verified runs here.** |
| `bin/inbharat-harness-debug` | x86_64-unknown-linux-musl | debug | ~19 MB | Same, with debug symbols for development |
| `bin/inbharat-harness.exe` | x86_64-pc-windows-gnu | release | ~787 KB | Windows x64 (or Wine). Real PE/MZ binary; **built here, not run here** (no Windows in sandbox). |
| `bin/inbharat-harness-macos-x86_64` | x86_64-apple-darwin | release | ~801 KB | Intel Macs. Real Mach-O; **built here, not run here**. |
| `bin/inbharat-harness-macos-aarch64` | aarch64-apple-darwin | release | ~764 KB | Apple-silicon Macs. Real Mach-O; **built here, not run here**. |
| `bin/hardening-c-abi-smoke` | x86_64 Linux (host) | smoke test binary | ~8.6 MB | C ABI hardening smoke test |
| `bin/libinbharat_harness.a` | x86_64-unknown-linux-musl | release static library | ~24 MB | Link into C/C++ programs via the FFI crate |

Per-target build evidence is generated by `scripts/build-targets.sh` and
recorded in `reports/TARGET_BUILD_EVIDENCE.log`. Evidence levels are stated
honestly: BUILT+RUNS (executed here), BUILT (produced and format-verified, not
run here), BLOCKED (cannot build in this environment, reason recorded).

## Quick start (Linux)

```sh
chmod +x bin/inbharat-harness

# What is this build?
bin/inbharat-harness info

# List commands
bin/inbharat-harness --help

# Deterministic routing demo
bin/inbharat-harness route "summarize this file"

# Interactive echo chat (local, no network)
bin/inbharat-harness chat

# Benchmark routing + false-activation set
bin/inbharat-harness benchmark
```

Secure defaults are read-only, no process spawn, no network, telemetry off.
Authority is opt-in: `--allow-write`, `--allow-process`, `--allow-program NAME`.

## Not included

- **Android** (`aarch64-linux-android`): BLOCKED in the build environment used
  here. zig 0.14.1 does not provide an Android libc, and the Android NDK could
  not be installed (no network route to it). The source compiles for the target
  up to the link step; an NDK toolchain is required to finish. Build with
  `cargo build --release --target aarch64-linux-android` on a host with the NDK
  and `CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_LINUX_ANDROID_LINKER` set to the NDK's `ld`.

Windows and macOS binaries ARE included (built and format-verified here), but
were not executed in the Linux-only build sandbox — treat them as BUILT, not
RUN-verified, until you run them on their native OS.

## Reproducing

The exact source that produced these binaries is in this same archive
(including full git history). To verify:

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl   # toolchain pinned by rust-toolchain.toml
cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
./scripts/check.sh                            # full lint+test+benchmark gate
```
